questions.q: In what order the reagents $N{a}_{2}S$ , $NaCl$ and $Nal$ are added to an aqueous solution containing ${\text{Ag}}^{+}, {\text{Cu}}^{+ 2}$ and ${\text{Ni}}^{+ 2}$ ions in order to precipitate $Ag^{+}$ first $Cu^{+ 2}$ second and $Ni^{+ 2}$ last.
questions.solution:
With $NaCl$ only $Ag^{+}$ precipitates $Ag^{+} + NaCl ↓ + Na^{+}$
With $Nal, Cu^{+ 2}$ precipitates $2Cu^{+ 2} + 4I^{-} \to C{u}_{2}{I}_{2} ↓ + {I}_{2}$
With $N{a}_{2}S, Ni^{+ 2}$ precipitates $Ni^{+ 2} + N{a}_{2}S \to NiS ↓ + 2Na^{+}$

questions.q: Gradual addition of potassium iodide solution to aqueous $Bi{\left(N{O}_{3}\right)}_{3}$ solution initially produces a dark brown precipitate which dissolves in excess of $KI$ to give a clear yellow solution. Identify the yellow precipitate.
questions.solution:
At first $Bi{\left(N{O}_{3}\right)}_{3}$ undergoes hydrolysis.

Nitric acid is formed which oxidises $I^{−}$ to iodine. The liberated iodine dissolves in $K$ to form yellow precipitate of ${KI}_{3}$ .

$Bi{\left(N{O}_{3}\right)}_{3} + {H}_{2}O \to \left[Bi\left(OH\right){ \left(N{O}_{3}\right)}_{2}\right] + HN{O}_{3}$

$2HN{O}_{3} \to {H}_{2}O + 2N{O}_{2} + \left[O\right]$

$2KI + {H}_{2}O + \left[O\right] \to 2KOH + \mathop{I2}_{Darkbrown}$

${I}_{2} + KI \to \mathop{K{I}_{3}}_{yellowsolution}$

(1) $Mn^{2 +}$ shows the characteristic green colour in the flame test

(2) only $Cu^{2 +}$ shows the formation of precipitate by passing ${H}_{2}S$ in acidic medium

(3) only $Mn^{2 +}$ shows the formation of precipitate by passing ${H}_{2}S$ in faintly basic medium

(4) ${\text{Cu}}^{2 +} | \text{Cu}$ has higher reduction potential than ${\text{Mn}}^{2 +} | \text{Mn}$ (measured under similar conditions)

\left(A\right)$ Manganese show pale purple colour in flame test.

\left(B\right)Cu^{2 +}\overset{{H}_{2}SHCl}{→}\mathop{CuS ↓}_{\text{Black ppt.}}$

\left(C\right)$ Both $Cu^{2 +}$ and $Mn^{2 +}$ form precipitate with ${H}_{2}S$ in basic medium.

\left(\text{D}\right){E}_{{\text{Cu}}^{2 +} | \text{Cu}}^{o} = + 0.34\text{V}, {E}_{{\text{Mn}}^{2 +} | \text{Mn}}^{o} = - 1.18\text{V}$

questions.q: Pick out the incorrect statement.
options: Mg also burns in gases such as $C{O}_{2}$ and $S{O}_{2}$

A. $Mg + C{O}_{2} \to 2MgO + C$
and $2Mg + S{O}_{2} \to 2MgO + S$

D. Inter-atomic forces (or metallic bonding) in alkaline-earth metals are stronger than in alkali metals.

questions.q: A solution of a metal ion when treated with KI gives a red precipitate which dissolves in excess KI to give a colourless solution. Moreover, the solution of metal ion on treatment with a solution of cobalt (II) thiocyanate gives rise to a deep blue crystalline precipitate. The metal ion is
questions.solution:
When a solution of a $Hg^{2 +}$ is treated with KI a red precipitate of $( Hg{I}_{2} )$ is obtained which dissolves in excess KI to give a colourless solution $( Hg{I}_{4}{)}^{2 -}$ . When the solution of $Hg^{2 +}$ is treated with a solution of cobalt (II) thiocyanate a deep blue crystalline precipitate of $Hg ( SCN{)}_{2}$ is formed. The reactions are as follows
$Hg^{2 +} + 2I^{–} \to Hg{I}_{2}$
$\mathop{Hg{I}_{2}}_{( excess )} + 2I^{–} \to \mathop{[ Hg{I}_{4}{]}^{2 –}}_{Soluble}$
${\text{Hg}}^{2 +} + \text{Co}{( \text{SCN} )}_{2} \to \mathop{\text{Hg}{( \text{SCN} )}_{2}}_{\text{Blue}\text{crystal}\text{line}\text{ppt} .}$

Here other ion $Pb^{2 +}$ , $Hg^{2 +}$ and $Co^{2 +}$ do not give precipitates formed in these reactions.

questions.q: The metal that produces red violet colour in the non-luminous flame is
questions.solution: Alkali metals and their salts impart a characteristic colour to flame. The reason for flame colouration is that the energy of the flame causes an excitation of the outermost electrons which on return to their original position give out the energy so absorbed in the visible region. So Rb gives a red-violet colour to the flame. Zn, Ag, Pb don’t show flame test as they have higher ionization energy so flame test is not possible.
